newsitem.title: ITALY: Kenyan drought could hit three million people - FAO.
newsitem.headline: Kenyan drought could hit three million people - FAO.

text.p: Kenya's government estimates that a drought which has wiped out crops could affect three million people and the country will need more food aid and grain imports than previously forecast, the U.N.'s food agency said on Friday.

The Food and Agriculture Organisation (FAO) issued a special news alert on the situation in the East African country, where it said the failure of rains had led to widespread crop failures and loss of livestock.
"The government estimates that some two million people are currently affected by the drought and that the number may reach three million if the situation persists," the FAO report said.
It estimated Kenya would need to import at least 1.3 million tonnes of food grains in the 1996/1997 marketing year, 200,000 tonnes more than the FAO previously forecast.
"This is almost double the average for the past five years," the report said.

It said an estimated one million tonnes would come from commercial imports but the bulk of the deficit could come only from international aid because of the low level of Kenya's stragetic food reserve and foreign exchange constraints.
"Substantial external assistance is therefore needed," the report said, noting that donor pledges at the end of last month amounted to only 43,000 tonnes.

Most parts of Kenya's North Eastern, Eastern and Coast Provinces and low-lying areas of its Central Province have been hit by drought after the failure of the short rains season, which normally starts in mid-October.
"For these same areas, the failure of the 1996/97 short rains follows two consecutive failures of the long rains (from March to May), thus worsening an already tight supply situation," the FAO said.

The outlook for short rains crops -- mainly maize, millet, sorghum and pulses -- has seriously deteriorated and the FAO will update production estimates and food aid needs in early April after its experts have visited drought areas, it said.
